coordination.lock.creation: created and fsynced with the store directory during explicit adoption
coordination.lock.lifetime: never unlinked, replaced, truncated or rewritten by an API, including recovery
coordination.lock.scope: every cooperative read, archive, pin, prune and recovery acquires this same stable inode before opening any owner guard

operation.lock.role: temporary owner authority and pre-commit failure guard; not the native mutex
operation.lock.removal: only after final protected data sync succeeds, while coordination.lock remains held
operation.lock.deletionDurability: not promised; a reappeared owner guard conservatively blocks normal operations and requires exact explicit recovery

phases: Acquire permanent native mutex; verify its inode, exact nonce payload and bounds.
Open/create and validate owner guard; validate recovery authority before dirty, preserving r3 refusal guarantees.
Execute unchanged source/archive/intent/manifest checks and durable mutation phases under both authorities.

After data and intent/marker cleanup checks, verify owner inode/token, sync store directory while both authorities remain, then verify owner binding again. This successful final sync is the data commit point.
Close owner handle, recheck owner path/bytes and unlink only that temporary guard while permanent native mutex remains held. Do not introduce another data/directory durability promise after deletion.
Release/close permanent native mutex. Its inode remains for every successor. No successor can acquire it during owner-path inspection/deletion.
failureRules: Source data writes, archive changes, intent/manifest/marker cleanup and final protected data sync failures are never classified as post-commit coordination-only errors.
Any such failure before owner removal retains the pre-existing owner guard, poisons the live instance and makes fresh verification incomplete even if diagnostic marker persistence also fails.
Owner-handle close or owner unlink failures preserve the still-existing guard, poison the instance and attempt a nonce/token marker without deleting original authority.

After confirmed data commit and successful owner removal, a native mutex unlock/close exception poisons the instance and attempts exclusive owner-guard recreation plus failure marker. These diagnostic writes do not undo the already durable data commit.

If every post-commit diagnostic write fails, a fresh process can see valid committed data but cannot discover the coordination-only exception. This limited observability is explicit and does not waive any pre-commit data failure obligation.
Cleanup exceptions cannot replace an earlier primary exception. Failed recovery never silently repairs authority, archive bytes, source facts or unknown commit outcomes.
A missing, symlinked or corrupt permanent mutex is incomplete and never automatically recreated. External operators must not replace its inode while any process may use the store.

oldCounterexample.oldPremise: directory sync is called after operation.lock was unlinked
oldCounterexample.r4Disposition: inapplicable because no such durability request exists; never report the original nine checks as passed
oldCounterexample.replacement: independent actual final guarded-sync failure and marker-write double failure with unchanged three safety obligations

newCases: actual final guarded data sync failure retains owner, poisons live instance and blocks fresh verification
final data sync plus marker create IO failure still retains original owner bytes
competing reader cannot return complete during final guarded sync
post-commit native unlock single failure restores owner guard and requires recovery
owner handle close failure retains original guard
owner unlink fails before unlink and retains original guard
reappeared temporary owner after nondurable deletion blocks until exact explicit recovery
foreign owner bytes at cleanup are not removed
secondary cleanup failure does not mask original operation exception
normal completion makes no new directory sync request after owner unlink
real thread recovery/reader competitors cannot enter owner-path deletion window; stable native inode remains
post-commit native release failure with all diagnostic IO denied preserves explicit fresh-observability boundary
missing or corrupt permanent mutex refuses before owner creation or source mutation

assumptionsAndLimits: The commit point means actual file fsync plus every platform-supported sync request completed. The frozen point.sync_directory invokes directory fsync on POSIX but is a controlled no-op on Windows; a Windows call or injected error is not physical directory persistence evidence.
Linux and Windows actual execution/fault receipts must remain separate. Physical disk power-loss and Windows directory-fsync certification are not executed or claimed.
Controlled local filesystem and cooperative API participants; no unobserved replacement of permanent mutex or source metadata while processes are active.
Scaled small-fixture faults are not maximum-size stress, OS hard resource quotas or physical power-cut certification.
Archive contents and original source guards remain verified; no archive deletion, automatic arbitrary SQL, list/relation closure or stable journal promotion is added.
